claim: Gurney Drive Hawker Centre hosts 50+ stalls along the seafront and is open daily from late afternoon to 1am; recommended stalls include #71/#107 for char kway teow and #79 for asam laksa.
quote: Gurney Drive Hawker Centre... 50+ stalls along Penang's northern seafront promenade, daily late afternoon through 1 AM. Stalls 71 or 107 serve Char Kway Teow... Stall 79 serves Assam Laksa

claim: Penang Road Famous Jin Kor Char Kuey Teow, located inside Joo Hooi Cafe on Penang Road, carries a Michelin Bib Gourmand and is a celebrity-favored CKT stall in George Town.
quote: Penang Road Famous Jin Kor Char Kuey Teow, PENANG – Popular With Celebrities With Michelin Bib Gourmand (In Joo Hooi Cafe)

claim: The legendary Air Itam Laksa stall by Ayer Itam market now opens only Saturday and Sunday 11am–6pm; founder Uncle Seong (Ang Kak Seong) passed away in April 2026 at 77 and the family is continuing the 70-year-old stall.
quote: Uncle Seong (Ang Kak Seong)... passed away in April 2026 at the age of 77... Opening Hours: Saturday & Sunday ONLY | 11:00 AM – 6:00 PM

claim: Nasi Kandar Line Clear at 177 Jalan Penang (junction of Chulia Street and Penang Road) operates 24 hours and has been a fixture since 1947.
Line Clear has faced repeated complaints in recent years about overcharging tourists, with reports of plates billed at RM57; locals advise asking for prices before ordering.
quote: reports of tourists being charged significantly more, including charges of RM57 for a plate

claim: The 2025 Michelin Guide for Kuala Lumpur & Penang named 56 Bib Gourmand eateries including 12 new entries; new Penang additions are BM Yam Rice, Laksalicious, Lum Lai Duck Meat Koay Teow Th'ng, Ravi's Famous Apom Manis, Serabai Istimewa, Super Star Koay Teow Soup and Winn's Cafe.
quote: In Penang, the inspectors selected BM Yam Rice, Laksalicious, Lum Lai Duck Meat Koay Teow Th'ng, Ravi's Famous Apom Manis, Serabai Istimewa, Super Star Koay Teow Soup and Winn's Cafe

claim: Siam Road Char Koay Teow holds a Michelin Bib Gourmand and is recognised in the Michelin Guide for its charcoal-wok-fried CKT.
quote: Siam Road Char Koay Teow – George Town - a MICHELIN Guide Restaurant

claim: Siam Road Charcoal Char Kway Teow trades from a roadside cart at 82 Jalan Siam Tue–Sat roughly noon–6:30pm and is closed Mondays and Sundays; waits can exceed an hour at peak.
quote: open Tuesday to Saturday from 12pm-6:30pm and is closed on Mondays and Sundays

claim: The Chulia Street Night Hawker cluster has relocated to Carnarvon Street and is busiest 6:30–8:30pm; Mother & Son Wantan Mee (nearly 50 years old) is a standout, with CKT plates RM8–9.
quote: the renowned hawker has shifted to Carnarvon Street... Mother & Son Wantan Mee stall is arguably serving one of the best wantan mee in Penang... small plate of the famed char kuey teow here is priced at RM8

claim: Bridge Street Prawn Noodle (Keo Thau Hokkien Mee) at 533 Lebuh Pantai is a Michelin Bib Gourmand stall known for combining prawn-mee broth with lor-mee gravy; open Tue–Sun 7am–2:30pm, closed Monday.
quote: Bridge Street Prawn Noodle, PENANG – Michelin Bib Gourmand Stall with Hokkien Mee + Lor Mee Gravy Combo

claim: 888 Hokkien Mee at 67-A Lebuh Presgrave has served prawn-noodle soup with pork rib and sambal for 30+ years; daily 3pm–9:30pm, closed Thursdays.
quote: 888 Hokkien Mee serves one of the most flavourful noodle soups in Penang, topped with pork ribs and sambal... operates daily from 3:00 PM to 9:30 PM, except on Thursdays

claim: Penang Road Famous Teochew Chendul on Lebuh Keng Kwee, in business since 1936, sells its signature shaved-ice cendol with coconut milk, gula melaka, kidney beans and pandan jelly noodles; diners eat standing or sit inside the adjacent Joo Hooi Cafe.
quote: Penang Road Famous TeoChew Chendul... started in 1936... Joo Hooi Cafe or bring your bowl and walk 2 stalls down

claim: Seng Thor Coffeeshop on the corner of Carnarvon and Kimberley Street has been frying oh chien (oyster omelette) since the 1930s and is a go-to George Town stop for the dish.
quote: Oyster Omelette (Oh Chien) That You Have To Try In Penang

claim: Penang Foodie's 2025 street-food roundup highlights the canonical local dishes a visitor should target: char kway teow, asam laksa, Hokkien mee, nasi kandar, char hor fun, oh chien, rojak, cendol and ais kacang.
